newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian wool prices ease at week's sales.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian wool prices ease at week's sales.

text.p: Australian wool prices eased on the last day of selling at sales this week in Newcastle, Melbourne and Fremantle, Australian Council of Wool Exporters said in its weekly market report.
The eastern market indicator rose three cents to 624 cents a kg clean. The western market fell one cent to 598 cents a kg.
A total 90,273 bales were offered, of which the trade bought 92.9 percent. The pass-in rate was 7.1 percent.
Trade competition was led by Japanese, Western European and Chinese buyers with good support from most sectors of the trade, the council said.

The council said the general concensus among exporters was that there was a correction or evening out of prices this week following an increase of nearly 30 cents in the eastern market indicator over the two preceding weeks.
"This rate of increase in prices could not be sustained under prevailing demand conditions," the council said.
Wool International said its stockpile of unsold wool totalled 1,849,330 as at February 27.
In the futures market, a total of 135 contracts were traded in the 21 micron contract in the week ended February 27.
Open interest decreased 41 contracts to close at 764.
The April contract closed down seven cents at 729 cents/kg clean.
The June contract also closed seven cents down at 744 cents a kg clean.
Sales next week are in Sydney, and Adelaide with a total of 39,876 bales rostered for sale.
